limitations: The interpretation of the repair coordinate as a potential is supplied explicitly as a test condition, not derived from native geometry.
Other physical fields, response variables, representations, or history-dependent rules require their own derivation.
The foundational identity test assigns neither physical duration nor physical measurability to an edge drop.

Carrying the fine contrast into a survivor's accessible record requires a rule for retaining or writing it as that edge disappears; a first arrival in the separate repair simulation does not supply this rule.
A coarse source observable intended to ignore the lost split has no obligation to carry that record.
proof_checks: The elementary leaf column of the native Laplacian correctly gives L e_u = e_u - e_p.
Direct evaluation correctly gives P(e_u - e_p) = 0, confirming the leaf-parent contrast survives P1.
The fine potential difference is correctly identified as the class [e_u], with an oriented drop from leaf to parent of exactly one.
Restricting to surviving vertices correctly gives the zero class, meaning every retained potential difference has zero contrast.
The repair difference between the parent p and the protected sibling w is a relative value, correctly invariant under common constant shifts.
After one archived sweep, the parent first coordinate is correctly calculated as f(7/20) for input a and f(13/40) for input b.
The contrast of the retained parent-minus-sibling difference is correctly evaluated as f(13/40) - f(7/20) < 0, relying on the strict monotonicity of f(t).
The original native retained potential gives zero for the same contrast, correctly demonstrating that the archived rule at default strength fails this direct potential identification.
The independent rational solutions and gauge shifts are correctly reconstructed and verified in the exact arithmetic cross-check.
